chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Sheffield's trial, transfer and later life as a photographer
summary: Sheffield, rumored to be the police chief's half-brother, escaped conviction, was moved from Central Avenue, then became a photographer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You know when they...when Sheffield was arrested and all that trouble and ever'thing, they played that record in the court ...to show his reputation. You didn't know that, did you?
I think I heard someplace that...was that the

SPIKES - 135
Reel 4
Page 29
same case that Dr. [H. Claude] Hudson was talking about?
I 'magine.
When he [Sheffield] was arrested and tried for having...
Takin' money from Chinamen or somethin', I think.

Oh, that was probably another case then. The one Dr. Hudson was talking about, the NAACP got involved with, was where he [Sheffield] killed an unarmed man, and then when his mother came to try to help...
He put his foot on her.
...he put his foot on her and hurt her hand, and ...and the...everybody was up in arms over Sheffield, and they...

I don't remember that exactly. I know that they had him down there. You know, if Sheffield was so big that, whenever they'd rent a...they tell me now when they...he was in with all the Chinese -- the gamblers. When they arrest them for the lottery and chuckaluck-- whatever they played and everything down there--when they bring 'em into court, he always got 'em out. See? And that's when it come out that he was a brother...he was a half-brother to the police chief at that...can't name...think of his name, either. I thought it was Davis, if I'm not mistaken but, Davis, I know there's another one later but I think that one at that time was named Davis, and they...they said he was a half-brother.
May have had something to do with the fact that, after that trial, he got...he was turned loose. He was free. He wasn't

SPIKES - 136
Reel 4

convicted of anything. There were all kinds of witnesses against him. Yeah, he wasn't convicted.
But, eventually, through pressure, they got him transferred to another part of town because people along Central Avenue...
I don't know why he got out of that. I can't remember. I don't whether they let him pension or whether...or whatever happened to him.
Well, Dr....Dr. Hudson says that he--after that trial, he got...Sheffield got assigned to the railroad yards and away from Central Avenue.
Maybe he did.

And then eventually, he retired, and that was when he became a photographer, opened a photography studio, and you were telling me that he was always on hand every time there was a picnic or a dance or any kind of event, Sheffield was taking pictures.
Yeh.
